title: Musicians who knocked him out in the twenties and thirties
summary: Bechet, Keppard, Hodges, Carney, Brown, Duke, Lester Young.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Who were some of the musicians who really knocked you out? Your career goes back to the twenties, and you were really, you know, sort of right in the development of this whole music. A lot of great musicians.
In the twenties I'd pick Sidney Bechet and Freddie Keppard, trumpet. And Johnny Hodges, saxophone, Art Carney on baritone sax --
I mean Harry Carney. And Lawrence Brown, trombone. Quite naturally, Duke. Lester Young. That knocked me out, playing with Les.
Yeah. That was '34, I think you said?
Yeah, '34, the year we played -- we had the accident and played --
